theory.intro: When two signs touch between numbers, replace them with a single sign.
steps: Find the two touching signs between the numbers.
Same signs (− and −) → write a single +.
Different signs (+ and −) → write a single −.

workedExamples.question_text:
Rewrite each expression with a single sign. Do not evaluate.
(a) $11+(-7)$
(b) $11-(-7)$
(c) $11+(+7)$
(d) $11-(+7)$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Different touching signs become $-$; same touching signs become $+$.
(a) $11+(-7)=11-7$
(b) $11-(-7)=11+7$
(c) $11+(+7)=11+7$
(d) $11-(+7)=11-7$

workedExamples.question_text:
Rewrite each expression with a single sign. Do not evaluate.
(a) $-13+(-9)$
(b) $-13-(-9)$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Keep the minus sign on the first number. Replace only the two touching signs between the numbers.
(a) $-13+(-9)=-13-9$
(b) $-13-(-9)=-13+9$

workedExamples.question_text:
Rewrite every touching pair with a single sign. Do not evaluate.
$-17+(-8)-(-6)+(+3)$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Replace each touching pair and keep the minus sign on the first number.
$-17+(-8)-(-6)+(+3)=-17-8+6+3$
